title: Luyện Đọc VSTEP: The Industrial Revolution (VstepR6-Test 01)

tasks.instructions: Directions: Read the passage and choose the best answer (A, B, C, or D) for each question.

passage.title: The Industrial Revolution
passage.text:
The Industrial Revolution, which began in Britain in the mid-eighteenth century and gradually spread throughout Europe and North America, fundamentally transformed human society. Prior to this period, most goods were produced by hand in homes or small workshops. The introduction of machinery — particularly the mechanized textile loom and the steam engine — dramatically increased production capacity and changed the nature of work forever.

The development of factory production concentrated workers in urban centers, leading to rapid urbanization. Cities grew almost overnight, creating both economic opportunity and acute social challenges. Workers, including women and children, labored long hours in often dangerous conditions for meager wages. This exploitation eventually gave rise to labor movements and trade unions, which fought for workers' rights and ultimately helped shape the modern social contract.

Beyond labor, the Industrial Revolution also triggered profound environmental changes. The burning of coal to power factories and locomotives released vast quantities of carbon dioxide and other pollutants into the atmosphere, marking the beginning of significant human impact on global climate. Rivers were contaminated by industrial waste, and urban air quality deteriorated sharply. Many historians now consider this period the genesis of the environmental crisis we face today.

Despite these negative consequences, the Industrial Revolution generated unprecedented wealth and technological innovation. Transportation networks — including canals and railways — connected markets and lowered the costs of goods. Agricultural productivity improved through better tools and methods. Over time, rising wages and falling prices for manufactured goods raised the standard of living for many people, though the benefits were distributed unevenly across society.
